paragraphs.title: The Wilderness Blossoms and Reveals God’s Glory

answers: They will be glad and blossom
easy.explanation: The KJV says that the wilderness and solitary place shall be glad, and the desert shall blossom.
easy.q: What will happen to the wilderness and the solitary place?

easy.explanation: Isaiah 35:1 says that the desert shall blossom as the rose.
easy.q: What will the desert blossom as?

answers: The glory and excellency of the Lord
easy.explanation: The passage says they shall see the glory of the Lord and the excellency of God.

medium.explanation: The desert will rejoice with joy and singing.
medium.q: What accompanies the blossoming of the desert?

medium.explanation: The passage mentions the glory of Lebanon and the excellency of Carmel and Sharon.
medium.q: Which fertile places are named in comparison?

medium.explanation: A solitary place is one that is alone, empty, or deserted.
medium.q: What does the word “solitary” most nearly mean in this passage?

answers: A barren place becomes a joyful, flowering place
challenge.explanation: The wilderness and desert change from barren places into places of beauty, joy, and singing.
challenge.q: What major change is described in these verses?

answers: They represent beauty, glory, and fertility
They are places the people must leave
challenge.explanation: These regions are used as examples of excellence and fertility.
challenge.q: Why are Lebanon, Carmel, and Sharon mentioned?

challenge.explanation: The word “singing” shows that the rejoicing is expressed through joyful sound.
challenge.q: Which word emphasizes that the joy is expressed aloud?

paragraphs.title: Encouraging the Weak and Promising Salvation

answers: The weak hands and feeble knees
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.”
easy.q: Who is told to be strengthened?

easy.explanation: They are told, “Be strong, fear not.”
easy.q: What are those with a fearful heart told not to do?

answers: He will come with vengeance and save His people
He will lead them into a dry wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse promises that God will come with recompence and save them.
easy.q: What will God do when He comes?

answers: Because God will come to save them
Because the land will become drier
Because they must abandon the way
medium.explanation: The promise of God’s coming and salvation gives them reason to be strong.
medium.q: Why are the weak encouraged to be strong?

answers: A heart filled with fear or discouragement
A heart that is physically strong
medium.explanation: The fearful-hearted are people who are afraid and need encouragement.
medium.q: What does “fearful heart” mean in this context?

answers: Strength, courage, and then the promise of salvation
medium.explanation: The people are first told to be strong, then not to fear, and then promised God’s salvation.
medium.q: What is the order of thought in these verses?

answers: Strength and courage are needed to overcome fear
They tell the people to exchange joy for fear
They command the people to stop walking
challenge.explanation: The command to be strong gives courage to those who are afraid.
challenge.q: How are “be strong” and “fear not” related?

answers: That He will come with recompence and save them
That He will send them back into the desert
challenge.explanation: The verse ends with the promise, “he will come and save you.”
challenge.q: What does God’s coming promise to the fearful-hearted?

answers: Fear and weakness contrasted with strength and salvation
challenge.explanation: The fearful and weak are called to become strong because salvation is coming.
challenge.q: What emotional contrast appears in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Human Healing and the Renewal of the Land

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened.”
easy.q: What will happen to the eyes of the blind?

answers: Waters and streams will break out
They will be filled with wild beasts
easy.explanation: Waters shall break out in the wilderness, and streams shall appear in the desert.
easy.q: What will happen in the wilderness and desert?

answers: The blind, deaf, lame, and dumb
easy.explanation: The verses mention the blind, deaf, lame, and dumb.
easy.q: Which people are specifically described as being healed?

answers: Both show salvation and new life
medium.explanation: People are healed while the dry land becomes full of water and vegetation.
medium.q: What do the healing of people and the renewal of the land have in common?

medium.explanation: The KJV says, “the parched ground shall become a pool.”
medium.q: What will the parched ground become?

answers: Places where water rises from the ground
medium.explanation: Springs are natural sources from which water flows.

answers: The blind eyes are opened; the parched ground becomes a pool
The desert blossoms; the eyes are closed
The deaf are silent; the streams dry up
challenge.explanation: The passage presents both human healing and the renewal of the land.
challenge.q: Which answer describes one change in people and one change in the land?

answers: Dryness is replaced by abundance and life
The wilderness has become more dangerous
The way is closed to the redeemed
challenge.explanation: Pools, springs, and streams show that the barren land has been renewed.
challenge.q: What does the appearance of water in dry places show?

challenge.explanation: Grass, reeds, and rushes are signs of flourishing vegetation near water.
challenge.q: Which detail joins the water and emphasizes the land’s fruitfulness?

easy.explanation: The verse says it shall be called “The way of holiness.”
easy.q: What will the highway and way be called?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “the unclean shall not pass over it.”
easy.q: Who shall not pass over the holy way?

easy.explanation: The next verse says, “No lion shall be there.”
easy.q: Which animal will not be there?

answers: The redeemed and those traveling toward holiness
medium.explanation: The way is for the redeemed, and those who walk in it will not go astray.
medium.q: For whom is the holy way especially intended?

medium.explanation: A highway is a main or raised road for travelers.
medium.q: What does “highway” mean in this passage?

answers: Safe travel without fear of attack
medium.explanation: Without dangerous beasts, the redeemed can walk there safely.
medium.q: What is made possible by the absence of lions and ravenous beasts?

answers: A special road set apart for holy travel
A road meant only for animals
A road no one may use
challenge.explanation: The way is set apart as holy and is intended for those who belong to God.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “The way of holiness” suggest?

answers: The unclean cannot pass, and dangerous beasts are absent
The unclean and beasts lead the travelers
The unclean and beasts protect the road
challenge.explanation: The way is protected both spiritually, by excluding the unclean, and physically, by excluding dangerous animals.
challenge.q: How does the passage address both uncleanness and danger?

answers: The way is clear enough that travelers will not lose their way
The road is full of confusing turns
Only animals can find the road
challenge.explanation: Even a foolish traveler will not err or go astray on this way.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “the wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err therein”?

paragraphs.title: The Joyful Return of the Lord’s Redeemed

easy.explanation: The verse says they shall return and come to Zion.
easy.q: Where will the ransomed of the Lord return?

easy.explanation: They will come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads.
easy.q: With what will the ransomed return?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “sorrow and sighing shall flee away.”
easy.q: What will flee away from them?

medium.explanation: They shall obtain joy and gladness, and everlasting joy will be upon their heads.
medium.q: What will accompany the ransomed on their return?

answers: People who have been rescued or redeemed
medium.explanation: The ransomed are those whom the Lord has rescued or redeemed.
medium.q: What does “ransomed” mean in this verse?

answers: Joy and gladness versus sorrow and sighing
medium.explanation: Joy and gladness come to the redeemed, while sorrow and sighing flee away.
medium.q: What is the main contrast at the end of the verse?

answers: It is described as lasting without end
It is brief and quickly disappears
It belongs only to the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The word “everlasting” emphasizes that the joy continues forever.
challenge.q: What does “everlasting joy” show about the joy?

answers: The redeemed travelers reach Zion with joy
The way is closed before the redeemed
challenge.explanation: The redeemed who walk the holy way are now described as returning to Zion joyfully.
challenge.q: How does this verse connect with the holy way in the previous verses?

answers: Sorrow and sighing give way to joy and gladness
challenge.explanation: The final verse describes sorrow and sighing fleeing as joy and gladness come to the redeemed.
challenge.q: What emotional change is described from sorrow to the final celebration?
